newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso hails Mercosur progress.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso hails Mercosur progress.

text.p: Brazilian president Fernando Henrique Cardoso on Tuesday hailed the Mercosur's progress in moving beyond a mere trade issues to problems that concern the lot of ordinary citizens.

Speaking at the opening of a Mercosur summit in the Northeastern Brazilian city of Fortaleza, Cardoso said the four country trade block had entered a new phase in which debate would begin to include social issues.
"The truth is we are beginning to grapple with integration at a human and social level," Cardoso said.
He said Mercosur negotiators were working on developing a common consumer rights code and harmonizing social security and labor legislation.
"In the modern world it is fundamental that we turn our attenion to the consumer, to the defense of ordinary people," said Cardoso.
In the five years since it was launched, the Mercosur customs union has become Latin America's most successful experience in economic integration.
Trade between the four partners has mushroomed to an annual flow of $15 billion this year from $5 billion in 1991.

Moreover, the three other Mercosur members -- Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay -- have become increasingly dependent on continued access to the vast Brazilian market, whose strength is the driving force behind the trade block.
Now these three countries are urging Brazil to further open its markets by lifting subsidies, deregulating government and creating a more competitive business environment.
Diplomats attending the Fortaleza summit said the theme of the meeting has been finding ways to build on the customs union structure to deepen the economic relationship.
"There has been a qualitative leap in negotiations," Jorge Cambell, the chief Argentine negotiator told Reuters.
"For the first time we are crawling inside one another's economy and saying this we like and this we don't."
Progress on consumer rights such as recognition of social security commitments and labor rights were all a part of this process, he said.

Later on Tuesday the four Mercosur presidents were scheduled to sign a free trade agreement with Bolivia, the latest country to forge stronger economic ties with Mercosur after Chile reached a similar agreement earlier this year.
